lHub.title: Running locally (overview)
lHub.body:
Download an open-weights model and run it yourself: data stays home, no per-token bill.

📍 Location: App overview › Run models locally › Running locally (overview)
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • A runner loads the model file into memory and computes on your machine.
  • Chat directly, or open a local API for your programs.

▶ How to use it

  • Check memory → estimate size → install a runner → download → run.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

For privacy, offline work, or tinkering.

✅ Why this works

Works offline; every setting is yours.

⚠️ Limits / notes: Models that fit a PC are usually weaker than the largest cloud ones; upkeep is on you.

lMem.title: Memory estimate
lMem.body:
Memory while running ≈ parameters × bits ÷ 8 + KV cache + the program.

📍 Location: App overview › Run models locally › Memory estimate
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Weights: an 8B model at Q4_K_M is about 4.6 GiB (llama.cpp figures).
  • The KV cache grows as the conversation grows.

▶ How to use it

  • VRAM is fastest; if it does not fit, runners can spill into RAM, but it slows down.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

If it does not fit, it will not run, or will be too slow to use.

✅ Why this works

A quick estimate saves downloading tens of GB for nothing.

⚠️ Limits / notes: Model shapes differ, so the KV cache is only a rough estimate.

lTool.title: Local runners
lTool.body:
Programs that run model files: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM.

📍 Location: App overview › Run models locally › Local runners
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Ollama: command line, local API on localhost:11434, OpenAI-compatible.
  • LM Studio: a desktop app; llama.cpp: the C/C++ engine; vLLM: a high-throughput server engine.

▶ How to use it

  • Beginners start with Ollama or LM Studio.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

They load files, handle quantized formats and drive the GPU, so you just use it.

✅ Why this works

With a local compatible API, cloud API code works after changing the address.

⚠️ Limits / notes: Runners differ in supported file formats and features.

lGguf.title: Model files and quant levels
lGguf.body:
In a file name, 8B, Q4_K_M and .gguf are the size, the quantization level and the format.

📍 Location: App overview › Run models locally › Model files and quant levels
⚙️ Usage layer: no model parameters change, only how you use it
🧪 Try it:

🎯 Role

  • Q4 ≈ about 4 bits per parameter; K is llama.cpp’s k-quant method; S/M/L are small/medium/large in that level.
  • GGUF is llama.cpp’s model file format.

▶ How to use it

  • In China, download from ModelScope or the hf-mirror mirror.

🧠 Why it’s designed this way (the logic underneath)

Fewer bits: smaller and faster, with slowly declining quality.

✅ Why this works

For the same model, Q4_K_M is roughly a third of the F16 size.

⚠️ Limits / notes: Commercial use depends on the licence on the model page.
